text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman discussed Bosnian elections in Zagreb on Tuesday "behind closed doors". The status of the self-styled Croat state, Herceg-Bosna, which was due to disappear by the end of August was also on the agenda.

- A legal vacuum in Bosnia won't be allowed. The actual institutions in Bosnia and the Serb entity will continue operating and they will have a role of supervisors until new joint institutions are set up, Michael Steiner, deputy to Carl Bildt's office in Sarajevo says.
- An initiative to establish six municipalities in the city of Mostar has been launched, Ivan Prskalo, mayor of Mostar says after meeting his deputy Safet Orucevic, former mayor of Mostar.
